rules.message: Handsontable 18.0 removed Numbro.js, so numericFormat.pattern does nothing. Replace it with Intl.NumberFormat options, for example style: 'currency' with currency: 'USD', style: 'percent', or minimumFractionDigits and maximumFractionDigits for a fixed number of decimals. Set the locale with the locale option. To keep Numbro, follow the Numbro recipe: https://handsontable.com/docs/javascript-data-grid/recipes/cell-types/numbro

Handsontable 18.0 removed Moment.js. A string dateFormat no longer works with the built-in date cell types: the option takes an Intl.DateTimeFormat object, for example { year: 'numeric', month: '2-digit', day: '2-digit' }, and the locale option picks the order. The source data must be ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD).

Handsontable 18.0 removed Moment.js. A string timeFormat no longer works with the built-in time cell types: the option takes an Intl.DateTimeFormat object, for example { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit', hour12: true }, and the locale option picks the style. The source data must be in 24-hour format, such as '14:30:00'.

Handsontable 18.0 removed DOMPurify and no longer sanitizes HTML. This grid passes markup to a surface that used to be sanitized (headers, menu labels, dialog or notification content, select options) and sets no sanitizer. If any of that markup is untrusted, add a sanitizer option, for example sanitizer: (html) => DOMPurify.sanitize(html). The codemod never adds one. Ignore this entry if you set the sanitizer elsewhere.

Handsontable 18.0 wraps the grid root in a new .ht-grid-content element and adds the .ht-slot-top, .ht-slot-bottom, and .ht-overlay siblings of .ht-grid. This selector depends on the old structure. Select by class instead, for example .ht-grid-content > .handsontable or .ht-wrapper.handsontable.

Handsontable 18.0 removed Pikaday. The date picker is now the browser's native date input, so the .htDatepickerHolder and .pika-* elements no longer exist. Remove this code, or style the native input instead.
